title: ACA s. 24 — Hearings and written proceedings

content.overview: Section 24 governs hearings and written proceedings, requiring an oral hearing when a party requests one unless the parties have agreed otherwise, subject to the statutory framework.
content.glance: Section 24 governs hearings and written proceedings, requiring an oral hearing when a party requests one unless the parties have agreed otherwise, subject to the statutory framework.
content.study:
Module 1: Hearing right
The tribunal determines whether proceedings are oral or written within the statutory framework; a party request for oral hearing must be treated according to section 24.

Module 2: Notice and participation
Parties must receive sufficient notice of hearings and meetings and an effective opportunity to participate.

Module 3: Efficiency
The tribunal may decide matters on documents where the statutory conditions permit, but efficiency cannot displace equal treatment and full opportunity.

examples.title: Rule applies
examples.body: A party requests an oral hearing and the statutory conditions for one are satisfied; the tribunal must apply section 24 accordingly.

examples.title: Rule fails or changes
examples.body: A tribunal disposes of a material dispute without hearing a party where the statutory framework requires an oral hearing.

hypotheticals.question: Does arbitration always require an oral hearing?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 24 permits written proceedings within the statutory framework, but an oral-hearing request can trigger the statutory requirement unless the parties agreed otherwise.

misconceptions.trap: Treating section 24 as self-contained without reading its statutory conditions.
misconceptions.correction: Apply section 24 with the Act's express conditions and connected provisions.
